author: zadjii-msft
title: Reloading extensions can drop all of an extension's commands when one item fails

judgment.rationale: The report provides a deterministic nested-command reload scenario and a concrete COM failure at PropChanged subscription. Current source confirms that DefaultContextMenuFactory initializes each context item without an item-level exception boundary, while CommandProviderWrapper.InitializeCommands invokes that initialization inside its top-level factory and LoadTopLevelCommands catches only at the whole-provider level. A single failure can therefore discard all commands from the provider.
evidence: The issue includes the COMException 0x800706BA at IWeakReference.Resolve while adding a PropChanged handler for a context item.
The reporter reproduced with ICommandProvider4.GetCommandItem, pinned nested commands, and multiple MoreCommands, and saw zero commands from the affected providers after reload.
DefaultContextMenuFactory.UnsafeBuildAndInitMoreCommands loops through context items and calls SlowInitializeProperties without a per-item catch.
CommandProviderWrapper.InitializeCommands creates top-level items via make in Select and pinned-command loops; CreateTopLevelViewModel initializes properties before returning.
LoadTopLevelCommands catches exceptions outside InitializeCommands, logs one provider-level failure, and does not preserve the successfully constructed sibling items.
The linked #41482 reports a different reload failure; its recent follow-up points to #46210 for a List capacity error, not this PropChanged RPC error.
judgment.recommended_action: Isolate initialization failures at the context-item boundary, clean up and log the failed item, and continue loading its siblings and unaffected provider commands.

fix_assessment.rationale: The failure boundary is directly visible in current source and a narrow per-item isolation change can retain healthy siblings without suppressing the error. The suspected stale CsWinRT weak reference remains an unverified underlying cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Isolate Command Palette context-item initialization failures
proposed_fixes.root_cause: A COMException while subscribing to one context item's PropChanged event escapes DefaultContextMenuFactory.UnsafeBuildAndInitMoreCommands. It propagates through TopLevelViewModel.InitializeProperties and the provider's top-level item construction, then reaches LoadTopLevelCommands' provider-wide catch, which leaves all commands from that extension unloaded. The stale weak-reference explanation is plausible but not yet confirmed.
plan: In DefaultContextMenuFactory.UnsafeBuildAndInitMoreCommands, catch failures for each ICommandContextItem independently, log the provider/command context and exception, clean up any partially initialized view model, and continue with sibling items.
Keep the parent command and successfully initialized MoreCommands available when one child fails; do not convert the failure into a successful empty context menu without logging.
Add a reload regression fixture with one context item whose PropChanged subscription throws and multiple healthy sibling/top-level commands; verify healthy commands remain available after reload.
verification: Reproduce the issue with a provider implementing ICommandProvider4.GetCommandItem, pinned nested commands, and multiple MoreCommands, then reload once or twice.
Inject or simulate a failure while one context item subscribes to PropChanged and verify the failed child is skipped while its parent, siblings, and other provider commands load.
Confirm the failure is logged with enough provider/command identity to diagnose it and that cleanup is performed for partially constructed view models.

confidence.rationale: The exception propagation and whole-provider catch are confirmed in current source, but the weak-reference lifecycle and best cleanup/retry semantics should be validated with a focused reload test.

issue_context.summary: A stale COM weak-reference failure while initializing one nested context item can abort the provider-wide command load during extension reload, leaving zero commands from that provider.
known_information: The developer report includes COMException 0x800706BA from IWeakReference.Resolve while adding PropChanged to a context item.
The repro uses an ICommandProvider4 provider with pinned nested commands and multiple MoreCommands; restart recovers the commands.
DefaultContextMenuFactory initializes MoreCommands sequentially without catching failures per item.
CommandProviderWrapper wraps provider loading in one catch around InitializeCommands, where the failing make operation can abort the provider's remaining items.
inferences: The stale CsWinRT event-source reference may survive extension process reload, but the issue has not established this as the root cause.
Per-item failure isolation should preserve healthy siblings even if the underlying COM failure recurs.
issue_context.analysis: The issue has a narrow, actionable resilience defect independent of whether the stale weak-reference hypothesis is correct: one failed context item currently escapes to a provider-level catch and discards all provider commands. Skip and clean up only the failing child, log the failure, and prove that healthy children and top-level commands survive reload.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body, repro, stack trace, suggested changes, labels, and the linked automated triage note.
Read current DefaultContextMenuFactory.UnsafeBuildAndInitMoreCommands: context items are initialized in a loop with no per-item catch or cleanup.
Read current CommandItemViewModel context initialization and CommandProviderWrapper.InitializeCommands/LoadTopLevelCommands: exceptions propagate to a provider-wide catch.
Compared #41482: its current follow-up concerns a separate capacity exception tracked by #46210, so it does not cover this RPC failure.

design.title: Isolate Command Palette context-item initialization failures

actions.label: Reproduce nested-command failure during extension reload
actions.note: The issue includes a specific extension shape and COM failure; confirm the failure boundary and healthy-sibling behavior before implementation.

reproduce.title: Verify per-item Command Palette reload isolation
reproduce.version_requirement: Current main or a build containing the current CmdPal extension host
prerequisites: At least two pinned nested commands, each with multiple MoreCommands context items.
steps: Load the extension and confirm its commands appear.
Invoke Reload Command Palette extensions once or twice.
Record whether one context-item PropChanged subscription fails and whether the provider reports zero commands.
Repeat with a controlled extension where one context item fails initialization and sibling/top-level items remain healthy.
reproduce.expected_result: A failed context item is logged and skipped, while its parent command, healthy sibling items, and other commands from the provider remain available after reload.
